Definition: Whether the system enables Know Your Customer (KYC) packet collection for service provision, particularly financial services
Comments: KYC is fully enabled via the National Identity Card. The Bank of Mauritius, Civil Status Division, Mauritius Police Force and MTCI signed MOUs for a Central KYC database via InfoHighway. Banks (e.g. MauBank) require NIC for customer onboarding. ICTA SIM Registration Regulations 2023 mandate NIC for SIM registration KYC. Smile ID provides digital KYC verification using NIC. MauPass e-KYC uses Acuant to compare selfies against NIC document photo.
revision_notes: All four cited sources were fetched and read. cseaafrica.org confirms it is a Mauritius-specific case study (InfoHighway, Data Protection Act s.3(4)(a), Digital Government Transformation Strategy) supporting inter-agency data exchange. MauBank FAQ confirms the NIC is a required KYC document for account onboarding. Smile ID confirms digital NIC-based identity verification for financial services in Mauritius (though the page mixes in unrelated Algeria content, its Mauritius-specific sections are consistent). OECD-OPSI confirms MauPass requires prior KYC registration for higher-assurance e-services. An independent search additionally confirmed the Bank of Mauritius signed MOUs with the Registrar of Civil Status, Mauritius Police Force and MTCI in April 2022 to establish a Central KYC system. Evidence supports Value Code 2 (Yes).
revised_comments: KYC is enabled through the National Identity Card. The Bank of Mauritius, the Registrar of Civil Status, the Mauritius Police Force and the Ministry of Technology, Communication and Innovation have signed memoranda of understanding to establish a Central KYC system accessible via the InfoHighway data-exchange platform, with the Bank of Mauritius Act amended to allow the Bank access to the Central Population Database for customer verification. Commercial banks such as MauBank require the National Identity Card for customer onboarding, and third-party providers such as Smile ID offer digital NIC-based identity verification for financial services. The ICTA (Registration of SIM) Regulations 2023 similarly mandate NIC-based verification for SIM registration.

Definition: Whether the civil registration and digital ID systems are integrated
Comments: Full integration. Mauritius has 100% civil registration coverage. A National Identity Number (NIN) is automatically computer-generated at birth registration (when at least one parent is Mauritian) and printed on the birth certificate. The same NIN is used on the national ID card at age 18, marriage certificates, and death deactivation — a complete lifecycle integration. The Civil Status Division manages both the CRVS and MNIC under the Prime Minister's Office, and data is shared via the Central Population Database and InfoHighway.
revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched. The id4africa presentation confirms the Civil Status Division (33 offices) manages civil registration, the National Identity Card and a Central Population Database, with 100% civil registration coverage. The PMO Annual Report confirms the Civil Status Division sits within the Home Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Office. A further check of the Civil Status Act 2023 (consolidated text) confirms section 8B establishes the Central Population Database populated automatically from birth registration with the NIC number, and section 8C grants the Bank of Mauritius statutory access for identity verification, corroborating full lifecycle integration. Value Code 3 (Full integration) is well supported.
revised_comments: The civil registration and digital identity systems are fully integrated. The Civil Status Division, within the Prime Minister's Office, manages both civil registration and the National Identity Card system through a single Central Population Database established under the Civil Status Act. A unique identity number is generated automatically at birth registration and carried through onto the identity card at age 18, marriage records, and death records, with civil registration coverage at 100%.

Definition: Whether procedural rules for collection, storage, and sharing of ID-related personal data are publicly available and established
Comments: Fully available data sharing rules. The Data Protection Act 2017 (Section 3(4)(a)) permits inter-agency data exchange on a need-to-know basis. The Digital Government Transformation Strategy and National Open Data Policy formalise data reuse. The InfoHighway platform requires MOUs/application forms, High-Level Management Team approval (chaired by MTCI), and data encryption for all 169 inter-agency connections. The Central KYC initiative (Bank of Mauritius, Civil Status Division, Police, MTCI) further governs financial ID data sharing.
revision_notes: Both cited sources were fetched and read in full. The cseaafrica.org case study (March 2024) confirms the Data Protection Act 2017 s.3(4)(a) permits need-to-know inter-agency exchange, and that the Digital Government Transformation Strategy 2018-2022 and National Open Data Policy 2017 are published documents governing data reuse. DLA Piper confirms the DPA 2017 framework. Independent verification of the InfoHighway platform (ih.govmu.org and its published leaflet) confirms a documented publisher-subscriber governance model requiring signed agreements and approval, with the case study specifically citing 169 active inter-agency connections as of March 2024. Value Code 3 (Fully available) is well supported.
revised_comments: Procedural rules for the collection, storage and sharing of identity-related personal data are publicly documented. The Data Protection Act 2017 permits need-to-know inter-agency data exchange, while the Digital Government Transformation Strategy and National Open Data Policy set out the government's data reuse principles. The InfoHighway platform operationalises this through a publisher-subscriber model requiring signed agreements or memoranda of understanding and central approval, connecting some 169 government agency systems.

Definition: Whether national data protection legislation exists and covers personal data linked to the ID system
Comments: The Data Protection Act 2017 (DPA 2017) came into force on 15 January 2018, repealing the 2004 Act. It aligns with EU GDPR principles, covers biometric data as a special category, mandates data controllers/processors to register, provides data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure), and requires 72-hour breach notification. Section 12 of the NIC Act explicitly subjects all MNIC data collection to the DPA.
revision_notes: Both sources were fetched and confirm the Data Protection Act 2017 came into force on 15 January 2018, repealing the 2004 Act and aligning Mauritius' framework with the EU GDPR. Value Code 2 (Yes) is confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Mauritius has enacted comprehensive data protection legislation. The Data Protection Act 2017 came into force on 15 January 2018, repealing the earlier 2004 Act and aligning the national framework with the EU General Data Protection Regulation, including provisions covering biometric data and data subject rights that apply to personal data held on the national identity system.

Definition: Whether a Data Protection Authority or similar body regulates ID data collection and sharing by the ID system
Comments: The Data Protection Office (DPO), headed by the Data Protection Commissioner, is the independent supervisory authority under the DPA 2017. It is under the aegis of the Ministry of Technology, Communication and Innovation but is fully independent operationally. It has powers to investigate complaints, conduct audits, issue enforcement notices, and oversee data protection compliance. The Data Protection Commissioner has publicly commented on compliance requirements for MNIC 3.0 and Mobile ID.
revision_notes: All three sources were fetched. DLA Piper and Appleby confirm the Data Protection Office, headed by the independent Data Protection Commissioner, is the supervisory authority under the DPA 2017. Le Mauricien (February 2025) confirms continued active engagement of the Data Protection Office with the Mobile ID rollout, including the Minister referencing Data Protection Office guidelines. Value Code 2 (Yes) is confirmed, with fresher evidence of active oversight.
revised_comments: A dedicated Data Protection Authority regulates identity-related data collection and sharing. The Data Protection Office, led by an operationally independent Data Protection Commissioner under the Data Protection Act 2017, has powers to investigate complaints, conduct audits and issue enforcement notices, and remains actively engaged in overseeing the rollout of new identity credentials such as the Mobile ID.

Definition: Whether the digital ID system is designed to be interoperable across government agencies and with other systems through APIs or data exchange protocols
Comments: The MNIC system is interoperable with other government systems via the InfoHighway platform, which connects 169 government agency connections (as of 2023). The Central Population Database (CPD), managed by the Civil Status Division, shares data with MRA, Ministry of Social Security, Bank of Mauritius (Central KYC), and other agencies. MauPass (launched 2020) uses CPD for citizen authentication across hundreds of e-services.
revision_notes: All cited sources were fetched. cseaafrica.org confirms InfoHighway facilitates 169 inter-agency connections as of March 2024, including the Central Business Registration Department, Civil Status Division, Economic Development Board, Mauritius Revenue Authority and National Transport Authority. OECD-OPSI confirms MauPass provides layered e-Authentication across government e-services using the Central Population Database. The id4africa presentation confirms Civil Status Division data sharing via InfoHighway. An official InfoHighway leaflet corroborates growth in connections over time (74 connections in 2019). Value Code 2 (Yes) is well supported.
revised_comments: The digital identity system is interoperable across government agencies. The Central Population Database, managed by the Civil Status Division, is connected to other agencies including the Mauritius Revenue Authority, the Economic Development Board and the National Transport Authority via the InfoHighway data-exchange platform, which facilitates around 169 inter-agency connections. MauPass, launched in 2020, uses the Central Population Database to authenticate citizens across a wide range of government e-services.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services
Comments: NIC use for banking is mandatory (for Mauritian citizens). Banks require the NIC for customer onboarding KYC. MauBank explicitly states that during customer onboarding, Mauritian nationals must use their National Identity Card (passport cannot substitute). The Central KYC database (Bank of Mauritius/Civil Status Division/MTCI MOU) further entrenches mandatory NIC-based KYC for financial services. The NIC number is required for National Savings Fund contribution records.
revision_notes: All sources were fetched. MauBank's FAQ confirms the Mauritian National Identity Card is a required KYC document for customer onboarding via its app. The consolidated Civil Status Act 2023 (section 8C) grants the Bank of Mauritius statutory access to the Central Population Database specifically for customer identity verification, providing a legal basis for mandatory NIC-based banking KYC. The cseaafrica case study corroborates the Central KYC initiative. The creolemauritius.com blog is a low-quality secondary source but is consistent with the primary evidence and was not relied upon alone. Value Code 3 (Mandatory) is supported by primary sources.
revised_comments: The National Identity Card is mandatory for opening bank accounts and accessing financial services. Banks such as MauBank require the card for customer onboarding, and the Civil Status Act grants the Bank of Mauritius statutory access to the Central Population Database to verify customer identity, underpinning mandatory NIC-based Know Your Customer checks across the banking sector.

Definition: Percentage of eligible population that has been issued or registered with digital ID credentials
Comments: Coverage exceeds 89% of the eligible population (citizens aged 18+). By June 2019, 1,666,808 Smart National Identity Cards had been issued, and enrollment is mandatory for all citizens 18+. Total population is ~1.27M (2024). As virtually all adult citizens are legally required to hold a card and the system has been operational since 2013, coverage of the eligible (18+) population is effectively >89%. A mobile team serves bedridden/disabled citizens for registration.
revision_notes: Both original sources were checked; the lawsofmauritius.gov.mu link is the National Identity Card Act text itself and does not contain coverage statistics, but the id4africa presentation was fetched and confirms 1,666,808 cards issued by June 2019 against mandatory enrolment for citizens 18+. A more recent and directly relevant statistic was found: the World Bank Gender Data Portal reports 99.1% of Mauritians aged 15+ held a national identity card or equivalent foundational identity document in 2021. This is a fresher, authoritative figure that confirms and strengthens the existing score. Value Code 5 (>89%) is confirmed.
revised_comments: Population coverage of the national identity credential is very high. According to World Bank data, 99.1% of Mauritians aged 15 and above held a national identity card or equivalent foundational identity document in 2021, consistent with mandatory enrolment for citizens aged 18 and above and a card issuance figure exceeding 1.6 million by 2019.

Definition: Whether credential is accepted or mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration
Comments: NIC is mandatory for SIM card registration. The ICTA (Registration of SIM) Regulations 2023 (effective 31 October 2023) mandate that all SIM holders register using their NIC (or passport for non-citizens). All existing SIM holders had to re-register by 30 April 2024. Operators (my.t, Emtel, Chili) verify NIC photo against the applicant's photograph. Failure to register leads to SIM deactivation.
revision_notes: Both sources were fetched. The ICTA FAQ confirms the Information and Communication Technologies (Registration of SIM) Regulations 2023 make SIM registration mandatory for all subscribers, requiring the National Identity Card (or passport for non-citizens/tourists) and photo verification against the ID. The Chili operator PDF confirms the regulations came into force on 31 October 2023, with all existing SIM holders required to re-register by 30 April 2024 or face deactivation. Value Code 3 (Mandatory) is confirmed.
revised_comments: The National Identity Card is mandatory for SIM card activation and mobile service registration. Under the Information and Communication Technologies (Registration of SIM) Regulations 2023, all mobile subscribers must register or re-register using their National Identity Card, with mobile operators verifying the applicant's photograph against the card and deactivating any SIM not re-registered by the regulatory deadline.
